title.narrative: APHRC - SRHR research to policy impact 2018-2024
APHRC - från SRHR forskning till policy-påverkan 2018-2024

description.narrative:
Insatsen avser stöd till African Population and Health Research Center (APHRC) för insatsen "Understanding the context of, and addressing sensitive sexual and reproductive health and rights issues in sub-Saharan Africa” 2018-2022.
Insatsen fokuserar på de mest omtvistade delarna av SRHR-agendan, särskilt rätten och tillgång till säker och laglig abort, ungdomars tillgång till SRHR-interventioner, inklusive sexualupplysning, och mänskliga rättigheter inklusive, yttrandefrihet och föreningsfrihet, samt tillgång till sexuella och reproduktiva och andra hälsotjänster för hbtqi-personer. Dessa tre delar av SRHR-agendan är mest eftersatta och möter störst motstånd på kontinenten.
Målet med programmet är att generera och stödja användningen av lokalt förankrad forskning och evidens för att förbättra inkorporering och genomföranden av globala och regionala SRHR-åtaganden i nationell lagstiftning, policy och riktlinjer för att på så vis öka tillgång till säker abort för kvinnor, öka tillgång till SRHR-interventioner för ungdomar och motverka social exkludering av hbtqi-personer.
Programmet förväntats bidrag till följande övergripande resultat:
• Regionalt och lokalt genererad policyrelevant forskning och evidens som kan ligga till grund för stärkt beslutsfattande, resursfördelning och implementering av policy och program för SRHR, som når alla populationer oavsett ålder, kön, sexuell läggning eller könsidentitet.
• Att kunskap och forskning i högre grad används som ett verktyg för att påverka och informera beslut som leder till bättre politik, smartare resursfördelning, som möjliggör skalbara och replikerbara SRHR-lösningar för förbättrad hälsa och välbefinnande för ungdomar och kvinnor som söker aborttjänster samt hbtqi-personer.
• Afrikanska institutionerna är bättre på att generera, tolka och använda forskning och kan därmed uppnå större påverkan i politiska processer, implementering och ansvarsutkrävande kring SRHR åtaganden.
APHRC kommer även att implementera programmet i Burkina Faso, Kenya, Liberia, Malawi, Rwanda, Sierra Leone och Zambia. Insatsen bidrar även till synergier med Sida/FORK:s stöd till APHRC för att bygga forskningskompetens, synergier till FORSK:s bilaterala stöd i Rwanda, samt synergier till Global Socials stöd till Guttmacher Institute enligt ovan.

The contribution aims to support APHRC’s programme titled “Understanding the context of, and addressing sensitive sexual and reproductive health and rights issues in sub-Saharan Africa” 2018-2022.
The contribution aims to address one of the slowest areas of progress in sub-Sarhan Africa, namely tackling the most sensitive parts of the sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) issues, particularly the right and access to safe and legal abortion, young people’s access to SRHR interventions, including comprehensive sexuality education, and the human rights and freedom of expression and association, and access to sexual and reproductive and other health services among LGBTI people. These are the three “most left behind” SRHR agendas.
The overarching goal of the programme is to generate and support the use of evidence to drive change and improve domestication and implementation of policies at national and regional levels that increase access to safe abortion for women and SRHR interventions for adolescents, and mitigate exclusion of sexual minorities. The programme aims to deliver the following three results:
• Impact 1: An African-generated corpus of evidence is at the basis of policymaking, resource allocation and translation of policy into best practice in SRHR, reaching all populations regardless of age, sex or sexual or gender identity. • Impact 2: Evidence is used as a tool to influence and inform decisions that ultimately result in better policy, smarter resource allocation, scale and replication of best practice in order to improve health and wellbeing outcomes for youth, women seeking abortion services and LGBTI people. • Impact 3: African institutions (researcher, decision-making and CSO-institutions) are better generators, interpreters and users of research and are using those skills to achieve greater impact in policy deliberations and execution of better practices
The regional work will harness synergies with existing Sida-supported programming at the level of the Southern African Development Community, East African Community and explore entry-points to the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) in order to meet identified evidence needs for improved policy formulation, implementation and resourcing within those economic blocs. It will also explore how evidence can support the domestication and implementation of global and regional policy instruments.
At national level, APHRC will implement the program in Burkina Faso, Kenya, Liberia, Malawi, Rwanda, Sierra Leone and Zambia – countries identified as presenting realistic opportunities to evolve the policy environment and enhance service delivery for liberal policymaking and implementation to reach adolescents with targeted SRHR services; improve access to safe abortion; and minimize the barriers that prevent LGBTI people from accessing basic services for health, education, livelihoods and well-being.

The goal of the Challenging the Politics of Social Exclusion (CPSE) project, managed by APHRC (African Population Health Research Centre), is to generate and support the usage of evidence to drive change and improve domestication and implementation of policies at national and regional levels that increase access to safe abortion for women, and sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) services for adolescents, and mitigate exclusion of sexual and gender minorities.

Between November 2018 and December 2024, the African Population and Health Research Center (APHRC) implemented the Challenging the Politics of Social Exclusion (CPSE) program. The below constitutes some examples of results that have been achieved during this period:
Long-term outcome 1: National, subregional, and regional policy actors seek and use relevant Africa-produced evidence in formulation, implementation and evaluation of policy and legislation on comprehensive SRHR and nondiscrimination of LGBTQI groups.
From 2022, APHRC shared evidence from the three studies on the lived experiences of pregnant and parenting adolescents in Burkina Faso, Kenya, and Malawi with a diverse range of policy actors, including members of parliament, ministries of health, the media, health care providers, CSOs, teachers, parents and parenting adolescents. Through engagement with these actors, the evidence generated has informed the inclusion of adolescent pregnancy in the National Council for Population and Development (NCPD) Kenya Strategic Plan 2023-2027, the Kenya National Population Policy for Sustainable Development (Sessional paper No. 1 of 2023), and the Kenya Adolescent Health Policy and Strategy (draft stage). In October 2022, APHRC shared findings from the Incidence of Abortion Study conducted in Sierra Leone with the Chief Medical Officer in the Ministry of Health, parliamentarians, CSOs, district and community health workers, religious leaders, and the media. This evidence was used by the CSOs to champion the Safe Motherhood Bill in parliament. The Bill has been gazetted and is undergoing validation by the ministerial cabinet. If passed, the Bill will expand access to abortion and post-abortion care services in the country.
Liberia has been on the verge of passing one of the most progressive laws in sub-Saharan Africa and APHRC has contributed to shaping the policy discussion by sharing its evidence and lessons from other regions. A joint study conducted by APHRC, CHAI, and the Ministry of Health the first nationwide study on abortion played a crucial role in influencing debates on access to comprehensive SRHR services. Notably, the study's findings shaped discussions on the draft Public Health Law and provided the lower house with a strong basis for passing the bill, which was later endorsed by the upper house. As a direct outcome of the study, the Ministry of Health has developed a Comprehensive Abortion Care Patients Register to help health facilities systematically track abortion and post-abortion complications and management nationwide.
Additionally, CHAI has implemented a flagship mentorship and training program for healthcare workers. The study also influenced the advanced implementation of the National Comprehensive Abortion Care Guidelines, and the Ministry is currently working on a Combi Pack Distribution guideline (to use a combination of two medicines: mifepristone and misoprostol).
Long-term outcome 2: Regional, subregional, or national level decision-makers shift behaviors, plans, or perspectives, toward advancing policy commitments on access to safe abortion and post abortion care, comprehensive adolescent SRHR services, and nondiscrimination of LGBTQI groups, based on evidence.
In Malawi, conversations and information-sharing around sex, adolescent and young women's pregnancy, abortion, and LGBTIQ inclusion have been hindered by taboos around discussions of sex and sexuality. Following a VCAT (Values Clarification and Attitude Transformation) training in 2022, health surveillance assistants in Blantyre gained comfort and leeway to speak openly with their communities on sensitive SRHR issues. The trained health surveillance assistants facilitated a 12-month life skills training intervention for adolescent mothers in Blantyre on their sexual and reproductive health.
In 2022, in collaboration with a Rwandan CSO, the team shared evidence from the Examination of LGBT Peoples Lived Experiences and Public Perceptions of Sexual and Gender Minorities in Rwanda Study and developed a digital story on sexual and gender minorities in Rwanda which reached a diverse audience through social media platforms. APHRC also undertook a stakeholder mapping exercise to understand the influences and interests of different stakeholders in the space. This prompted a broader reflection on how to integrate such insights into advocacy and stakeholder engagement campaigns. The team also strengthened the capacities of CSOs and the media on human rights-based approaches, policy and media advocacy and VCAT. This empowered the CSOs to produce a common advocacy strategy on LGBTQI rights. The team further worked with the Rwandan CSO to conduct dialogue workshops with parents, local leaders and law enforcement agencies, with those participating in these dialogues sharing their greater understanding and appreciation of the need to respect the rights of LGBTQI individuals.
Kilifi County in Kenya has recently made significant progress in maternal, child, and newborn health and has developed the Reproductive, Maternal, Neonatal, Child, and Adolescent Health (RMNCAH) Bill 2024. Building on the successful collaboration in organizing Kilifi Countys 2nd Scientific Symposium in 2023, APHRC co-convened a multistakeholder dialogue in 2024 that brought together representatives from the Kilifi County Department of Health, healthcare providers, and the County Assembly to discuss strategies for reducing maternal mortality and morbidity, as well as improving access to safe abortion and PAC services. During the two-day dialogue, stakeholders discussed practical strategies to achieve the target of 70 maternal deaths per 100,000 live births. The session concluded with commitments from participants to enhance maternal health services, update legal frameworks, and improve healthcare service delivery infrastructure, ensuring a collaborative effort to address maternal health challenges comprehensively.
